timeline.title: Thomas Markle Sr. Arrested in Florida on Child Abuse Material Charges
timeline.summary: Thomas Markle Sr., the estranged father of Meghan Markle, was arrested by federal agents in Florida on charges related to the possession of child sexual abuse material. The arrest follows an investigation that began after his son reportedly discovered boxes containing numerous images at his father's former home in the Philippines. Meghan Markle expressed that she is 'deeply distressed' by the charges against her father.

event_overview.title: About Child Abuse
event_overview.subject: Child Abuse
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a federal criminal case involving Thomas Wayne Markle, who was arrested on November 6, 2026, on a complaint alleging possession of child sexual abuse material. The case arose from an FBI investigation and searches of two Los Angeles-area storage units; the allegations have not been adjudicated, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

facts.label: Date and procedural status
facts.value: Federal authorities announced Markle's arrest on November 6, 2026. He was expected to make an initial appearance in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida in Tampa.

facts.label: Charging authority and venue
facts.value: The matter was announced by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California and is based on a federal criminal complaint charging one count of possession of child pornography.

facts.label: Alleged investigative basis
facts.value: According to the Justice Department, agents searched two storage units registered to Markle after receiving information in October 2026, and seized approximately 78 items—including slides, film negatives and books—that contained suspected child sexual abuse material.

facts.label: Legal stakes
facts.value: The Justice Department says a conviction on the charged offense could carry a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison; a criminal complaint is an allegation rather than a finding of guilt.

facts.label: Relevant terminology
facts.value: Florida law-enforcement guidance defines child sexual abuse material as visual depictions of sexually explicit conduct involving a person under 18, and states that possession, distribution, transmission and manufacture are illegal under Florida law.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the October 2026 reporting about earlier allegations and the November 6 federal arrest, but does not establish the truth of the allegations, resolve the criminal case, or provide a complete account of all related investigations.
